title: C#: FATAL CRASH_COND on handle mismatch in unmanaged_instance_binding_create_managed, plus repeated "Handle is not initialized" errors after a cleared binding handle
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: Godot `4.7.2.stable.mono` (built from the official 4.7.2 sources, engine commit `ed1daf0bf001b61586d9930840f2f1394092c079`), .NET 10, `--headless`, Linux x86_64.
- Verified today against `master` sources: the three code paths below are unchanged, so this is not fixed.

### System information

Linux (x86_64, Arch-based) - Godot v4.7.2.stable.mono - headless (dummy renderer) - .NET 10 runtime

### Issue description

A single broken `CSharpScriptBinding` state (native type `WEAK_HANDLE`, handle pointer `nullptr`, `inited == true`) produces three observable failures, one of which aborts the process.

**A. `Handle is not initialized` when the managed side of a weak handle was already collected** - thrown from `ScriptManagerBridge.SwapGCHandleForType()`, reached from native `CSharpInstance::refcount_incremented()`. Once a binding is in this state the error repeats on **every** later reference-count increase of that object (9 consecutive errors inside one cycle in one of my app-side runs).

**B. The same error from the binding-free path** - `CSharpLanguage::_instance_binding_free_callback()` calls `SetGodotObjectPtr(script_binding.gchandle.get_intptr(), nullptr)`, so a cleared handle is handed to `GCHandle.FromIntPtr()` there too.

**C. Process abort** - `ERROR: FATAL: Condition "gchandle.get_intptr().value != p_old_gchandle.value" is true.` followed by `handle_crash: Program crashed with signal 4` in `godotsharp_internal_unmanaged_instance_binding_create_managed()`. The line carries the engine's own `// TODO: Possible data race?`. It is reached from managed object-id resolution (`GodotObject.InstanceFromId()` / `IsInstanceIdValid()` -> `InteropUtils.UnmanagedGetManaged()`), and in the reproducer below it also shows up as `signal 11` instead of the FATAL condition.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Gist (5 files): https://gist.github.com/lunemoe/d36c4484d44f0243cb4eac5cc5ccb877

```
dotnet build
Godot --headless --path .
```

Phase A (deterministic handle error):
1. `GD.Load<Theme>("res://payload_theme.tres")` - cached resource, reference count 1 while the managed wrapper holds it.
2. attach it to a persistent node (count 2), wait one frame.
3. detach it (`node.Theme = null`, count 1) - `CSharpInstance::refcount_decremented()` turns the strong handle into a weak one.
4. drop the last managed reference so the wrapper is unreachable.
5. `GC.Collect()` - the wrapper is collected (the weak handle's target is gone) but its finalizer has not run yet.
6. re-acquire the same cached object with `GD.Load<Theme>(...)` - `refcount_incremented()` then runs the weak->strong swap against a collected target.

Phase C (abort): create batches of `new Gradient()` resources, drop them, `GC.Collect()` to queue their finalizers, then resolve their ids from the main thread (`GodotObject.InstanceFromId()` / `IsInstanceIdValid()`) while the finalizer thread is releasing the same objects' bindings.

Observed on Godot 4.7.2.stable.mono, headless, one process per run:
- **10/10 runs aborted**: 9x the FATAL condition above (signal 4) and 1x `Program crashed with signal 11`.
- Phase A emitted **5-50 `Handle is not initialized` errors per run**, always from `ScriptManagerBridge.SwapGCHandleForType()`.
- Manifestation B appeared in 1 of the 10 runs.

Control that pins the window in phase A: adding `GC.WaitForPendingFinalizers()` **before** the re-acquire makes the same project emit **0 errors** (2/2 runs). The failing state therefore needs the wrapper collected while its finalizer is still pending - which also explains why this is intermittent in real projects.

An app-side stress reproducer (a large scene graph with shared cached resources, 32 load/instantiate/free cycles per process) hits A in 4 of 13 runs and C in 1 of 13; the MRP above is the reduced form.

### Analysis

`CSharpInstance::refcount_incremented()` (`modules/mono/csharp_script.cpp`, 4.7.2 line 1847, failure branch line 1871) clears the handle before the swap and returns early when the swap fails:

```cpp
GCHandleIntPtr old_gchandle = gchandle.get_intptr();
gchandle.handle = { nullptr }; // No longer owns the handle (released by swap function)
...
bool target_alive = GDMonoCache::managed_callbacks.ScriptManagerBridge_SwapGCHandleForType(
        old_gchandle, &new_gchandle, create_weak);
if (!target_alive) {
    return; // Called after the managed side was collected, so nothing to do here
}
gchandle = MonoGCHandleData(new_gchandle, gdmono::GCHandleType::STRONG_HANDLE);
```

`MonoGCHandleData::is_weak()` (`modules/mono/mono_gc_handle.h` line 67) only inspects the stored type, so the binding keeps reporting "weak" while its pointer is null. Every later increase takes the same branch and passes a null handle to `SwapGCHandleForType()`, whose first statement is `GCHandle.FromIntPtr(oldGCHandlePtr)` (A); the binding-free path passes the same null handle to `SetGodotObjectPtr()` (B); and `runtime_interop.cpp` line 269/270 compares the caller's handle with the binding's current handle with a `CRASH_COND` (C):

```cpp
	// TODO: Possible data race?
	CRASH_COND(gchandle.get_intptr().value != p_old_gchandle.value);
```

For reference, `GCHandle.FromIntPtr(IntPtr.Zero)` throwing `InvalidOperationException: Handle is not initialized.` is easy to confirm in a plain .NET app; that is the exact message all three paths surface.

This looks related to #112067 (same failure branch, confirmed/open). It is filed separately because of the additional abort path and because the binding stays broken permanently once it has been hit.

### Logs

(1) Manifestation A from the MRP:
